newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia PM says to raise madcow issue in Belgium.
newsitem.headline: Russia PM says to raise madcow issue in Belgium.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Friday he would raise the issue of illegal British beef exports entering Russia disguised as Belgian produce when he visits Belgium next week.

"Russia will brook no compromises on the issue of tough veterinary control of the quality of meat bought abroad," Itar-Tass news agency quoted him as saying during a visit to the town of Sarov some 400 km (250 miles) southeast of Moscow.
"The Russian government intends to raise the issue in a firm manner with the Belgian authorities in order to avoid any repetition of the incident," he said.
On Thursday Agriculture Minister Viktor Khlystun said that Russia had imported 730 tonnes of British beef, which is subject to a worldwide ban because of mad cow disease.
He did not give a precise date for the import of the beef, which he said came via Belgium, nor did he say to where in Russia it was delivered.
The announcement marked the first time the Russian government has recognised the import of large quantities of banned beef. Officially, Russia has not imported British beef since 1990.
The European Commission said last week that 1,600 tonnes of British beef had been illegally exported to the Netherlands, Russia and Egypt through Belgium.
German authorities this week seized an unspecified quantity of beef imported from Belgium which they believed came illegally from Britain. They said it was heading for Russia via Germany.
Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), or mad cow disease, has been linked to a handful of deaths in Britain from Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease among people believed infected by eating beef.
